races.name: Dwarves of the Iron Hills

traits.name: Ability Score Increases
traits.description: Your Constitution and Strength scores increase by 2.

traits.name: Adventuring Age
traits.description: 50 to 100. Dwarves generally start their life on the road in their fifties, and do not usually consider retiring before their nineties. Around that time, they feel they can no longer stay away from their family, or want to dedicate themselves solely to the perfection of their crafts. But Dwarves can remain active until they are more than two hundred years old, and may return to adventuring if a great need arises, like the opportunity to avenge an old insult or injury, or to recover a treasure or reclaim a long-lost dwarf-hold. A healthy Dwarf who avoids a violent death can reach two hundred fifty years of age.

traits.name: Size
traits.description: Dwarves generally stand between 4 to 5 feet tall and can weigh upwards of 160 lbs. Your size is Medium.

traits.name: Speed
traits.description: Your base walking speed is 25 ft. Your speed is not reduced by wearing heavy armour.

traits.name: Night Vision (Dwarf)
traits.description: Accustomed to life underground, you have superior vision in dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 ft of you as if it were bright light, but you cannot see in the dark.

traits.name: Dwarven Resilience
traits.description: You have advantage on saving throws against poison, and you have resistance against poison damage.

traits.name: Tools for War
traits.description: You have proficiency with axes, hand-axes, great axes, hammers, mattocks and warhammers.

traits.name: Tool Proficiency
traits.description: You gain proficiency with the artisan’s tools of your choice: jeweller’s tools, mason’s tools, miner’s tools, smith’s tools, or woodcarver’s tools. You also gain proficiency in one musical instrument of your choice.

traits.name: Stonecunning
traits.description: Whenever you make an Intelligence (History) check related to the origin of stonework, you are considered proficient in the History skill and add double your Proficiency Bonus to the check, instead of your normal Proficiency Bonus.

traits.name: Languages
traits.description: You can speak, read, and write Dalish, which is the tongue of the Bardings, who speak an older version of the Common Tongue. You can also speak, read and write the secret language of your people, which has never been shared with any others.

traits.name: Sworn Allegiance
traits.description: "We are hastening to our kinsmen in the Mountain, since we learn that the kingdom of old is renewed." Your do not give your trust to others easily, but when it happens, the bond that is formed is so strong that you treat your friends as kinsmen. The first time that you complete a long rest during an Adventuring phase you gain Inspiration as long as your companions are not Paralysed, Petrified, Poisoned, Miserable, Stunned or Unconscious. If at least half of the Company are Dwarves, you gain Inspiration in this manner after each long rest, not just the first one.

traits.name: Ironfoot Hauberk (Ring-mail)
traits.description: The ancient weaponsmiths of your folk possessed the secret of forging a hauberk of steel mail, made of a fine and flexible mesh that is especially comfortable and lightweight (for a suit of metal armour). You do not have Disadvantage on Stealth checks when wearing the Ironfoot Hauberk. Furthermore, if you have Dexterity of 12 or higher, the armour provides AC 15.

races.description: The Dwarves of the Iron Hills are a hardy breed of Dwarves who live the simple but harsh life of miners and smiths, often gruff and terse with outsiders. They sport long, forked beards, plaited and thrust into their belts when they travel, fight or work the forge.

Speed.notes: Speed is not reduced by wearing heavy armor

Night Vision (Dwarf).notes: Can see in dim light within 60 ft as if it were bright light, but cannot see in darkness (not darkvision)

Dwarven Resilience.notes: Advantage on saving throws against poison

Stonecunning.notes: Considered proficient in History for Intelligence (History) checks related to origin of stonework, and adds double proficiency bonus instead of normal proficiency bonus

Languages.notes: Can speak, read, and write Dalish and the secret language of the dwarves

Sworn Allegiance.notes: Gain Inspiration after first long rest during an Adventuring phase if companions are not Paralysed, Petrified, Poisoned, Miserable, Stunned, or Unconscious; if at least half the Company are Dwarves, gain Inspiration after each long rest

Ironfoot Hauberk (Ring-mail).notes: No disadvantage on Stealth checks when wearing Ironfoot Hauberk; if Dexterity is 12 or higher, the armor provides AC 15

races.name: Dwarves of the Grey Mountains

traits.description: Your Constitution score increases by 2 and your Wisdom increases by 1.

A healthy Dwarf who avoids a violent death can reach two hundred fifty years of age.

traits.description: Dwarves generally stand between 4 to 5 feet tall and can weigh upwards of 160 lbs. Your size is Medium.

traits.name: Speed
traits.description: Your base walking speed is 25 ft. Your speed is not reduced by wearing heavy armour.

traits.name: Night Vision (Dwarf)
traits.description: Accustomed to life underground, you have superior vision in dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 ft of you as if it were bright light, but you cannot see in the dark.

traits.name: Stonecunning
traits.description: Whenever you make an Intelligence (History) check related to the origin of stonework, you are considered proficient in the History skill and add double your Proficiency Bonus to the check, instead of your normal Proficiency Bonus.

traits.name: Born to the Road
traits.description: You have proficiency in the Survival skill. When beginning a journey where you serve as Guide for the Company, you may spend Inspiration instead of making an Embarkation Roll. You may choose one of the following results: Fine Weather, Paths Both Swift and True or Hidden from the Shadow.

traits.name: Languages
traits.description: You can speak, read, and write Dalish, which is the tongue of the Bardings, who speak an older version of the Common Tongue. You can also speak, read and write the secret language of your people, which has never been shared with any others.

races.description: Dwarves of the Grey Mountains are a sturdy folk of stone and iron, dwelling in the cold halls beneath the Grey Mountains. They are known for their craftsmanship, resilience, and deep grudges.

Speed.notes: Speed is not reduced by wearing heavy armor

Night Vision (Dwarf).notes: Sees in dim light within 60 ft as if bright light, but cannot see in darkness (not true darkvision)

Dwarven Resilience.notes: Advantage on saving throws against poison

Tool Proficiency.notes: Choose one artisan's tool from the list; also gain one musical instrument of choice

Stonecunning.notes: Treated as proficient in History for Intelligence (History) checks related to stonework, and adds double proficiency bonus instead of normal proficiency bonus

Born to the Road.notes: When serving as Guide for the Company at the start of a journey, may spend Inspiration instead of making an Embarkation Roll and choose Fine Weather, Paths Both Swift and True, or Hidden from the Shadow

Languages.notes: Can speak, read, and write Dalish and the secret language of the dwarves

magic_items.name: The Arkenstone of Thráin
magic_items.description: Found in the deep mines of Erebor in the earliest days of the Dwarf-hold's founding, this pale jewel – known as "the Heart of the Mountain" – is the greatest treasure ever unearthed by the Dwarves. The skill of the Dwarf-smiths transformed the already beautiful stone into a fist-sized orb, with a thousand flawless facets; it shines with an inner luminescence, but when the merest sliver of outer light falls upon it, it gleams like water in the sunlight, shot through with the colours of the rainbow. In the centuries after its discovery, the Arkenstone became an heirloom of the Kings of Durin's folk. Thráin's son, Thorin, carried it away into the Grey Mountains where it remained until King Thrór brought it back to the Great Hall of Thráin. When the Dragon Smaug sacked Erebor, the Arkenstone was thought lost, lying among Smaug's treasure trove in the bottommost cellar until Bilbo Baggins discovered it and gave it to Bard. After the Battle of Five Armies, enmity was set aside between the leaders of the Dwarves, Elves and Men, and Bard of Dale placed the Heart of the Mountain in Thorin's tomb. Nearly a thousand years after its discovery, the Arkenstone is buried once more beneath the Lonely Mountain. The Arkenstone is a Wondrous Artefact with a Greater Blessing of Intimidation (See the Loremaster's Guide, page 127).

magic_items.name: Runes of Resilience
magic_items.description:
Craftsmanship: Dwarven 
Item: Armour, Helm 
This particular set of armour is engraved with runes of protective magic that assist the wearer in recovery. 
While wearing armour with this Enchanted Quality, you have Advantage on death saving throws.

magic_items.name: Venomed
magic_items.description:
Craftsmanship: Dwarven 
Item: Close combat weapon 
Old legends preserved in the chamber of records in Erebor and whispered among the Northmen tell how Dwarves of Eastern mansions came under the Shadow and turned to evil. No one is alive today who could confirm such tales, but in treasure-hoards it is still possible to find instruments of war of Dwarven craftsmanship, marked with baleful runes that no smith of Durin’s folk would confess to know; engravings capable to make a foe sick. 
When you are using a weapon bestowed with this Quality and you inflict damage on an adversary for the first time, your foe is considered to be Poisoned for a number of rounds equal to your Shadow rating (minimum of 1 round). Using this weapon against those who do not serve the Enemy directly (for example, against misguided Men or beasts who are defending their home or young) is a Misdeed worthy of Shadow points.

magic_items.name: Agarial
magic_items.description:
Type: Short sword 
Craftsmanship: Dwarven (Nogrod) 
Qualities: 1. Masterpiece 2. Fierce 3. Superior Fell 
Notes: A blade thought lost forever at the end of the First Age and forged as part of a set of similar weapons by Telchar himself, Agarial is akin to the blade used by Beren to steal the Great Jewel from the Iron Crown of Morgoth. Though it is an instrument of death, Agarial is a thing of surpassing beauty, a work of skill without peer in the world today.

magic_items.name: The Black Axe of Beleriand
magic_items.description:
Type: Great Axe 
Craftsmanship: Dwarven (Nogrod) 
Qualities: 1. Grievous 2. Superior Keen 3. Venomed 
Notes: A dangerous blade whose tragic history is one of great deeds and terrible sorrow, the Black Axe was wielded by many chieftains of the Edain in the First Age.

magic_items.name: The Shield of Anar (Rhingalad)
magic_items.description:
Type: Shield 
Craftsmanship: Dwarven (Khazad-dûm) 
Qualities: 1. Cunning Make 2. Superior Reinforced 3. Blessing: Inspire 
Notes: A sturdy shield forged from iron and embossed with gleaming ithildin runes, the Shield of Anar burns with a cold light which, in the hands of the right hero, hardens resolve and lifts the hearts of others, driving them on to valiant deeds. Called Rhingalad by the Elves and still sung of in song, it disappeared during the fall of Eregion. At the time its bearer, Anar the True, gave his life so that the last children of Hollin could flee safely with Elrond of Rivendell.

magic_items.name: War-mask of Belegost
magic_items.description:
Type: Helm 
Craftsmanship: Dwarven (Belegost) 
Qualities: 1. Runes of Resilience 2. Gleam of Terror 3. Fireproof 
Notes: A headpiece worn by a legendary Dwarf-lord, this helm incorporates a full faceplate intricately engraved to look hideous and grotesque, revealing only a glint of its wearer’s eyes when worn. The helm has what appears to be scorch marks covering it that neither craft nor magic can remove, yet it is otherwise unmarred.

magic_items.name: Angrenithil
magic_items.description:
Type: Long Sword 
Craftsmanship: Dwarven (Khazad-dûm) 
Banes: Orc-kind 
Qualities: 1. Grievous 2. Foe-slaying 3. Superior Fell 
Notes: Forged in the final century before the fall of Eregion, Angrenithil is made of shining steel and Mithril, though this is only evident by moon or starlight when the blade’s runes glow in the dark. Forged in friendship between a great Dwarven and Elven smith, bound with their mutual hatred of their chief foes, the blade is truly perilous to Orcs. Though Angrenithil is long lost, the Goblins of the Misty Mountains fear it still. In their rough tongue they name it “moon shanker” and they curse it, along with anyone who may bear it.

magic_items.name: Drake-bane
magic_items.description:
Type: Spear 
Craftsmanship: Dwarven (Erebor) 
Banes: n/a 
Qualities: 1. Grievous 2. Superior Keen 
Notes: When Dwarves forge arms for their own use, they generally prefer to craft weapons other than spears. But during their struggle with the Dragons in the Grey Mountains, they found it prudent to not always draw close to their scaled foes. This is but one of a number of spears that was forged with similarly optimistic names.

magic_items.name: A set of keys forged of a variety of precious metals
magic_items.description: A set of keys forged of a variety of precious metals. The keys range in size from those used to open a locket to a massive key that must have opened an equally massive lock and door. The larger keys are decorated with geometric designs of inlaid gemstone dust, precious metals and rare minerals.

magic_items.name: Dragon-bane
magic_items.description: In a past age, the Elves and the Dwarves found themselves with a common enemy and bent their prodigious skills to creating weapons that might slay a Great Worm. In the Third Age, such weapons are all but lost, in no small part due to the efforts of the Dragons themselves. A Legendary Weapon of either Elven or Dwarven Craftsmanship may have Dragons selected as its Bane creature, as described on page 133 of the Loremaster's Guide.

magic_items.name: Dragon-scale Brooch
magic_items.description: A small brooch fashioned from part of a Dragon's scale, supposedly from Scatha himself. (Contains a Greater Blessing of Riddle, see page 127 of the Loremaster's Guide.)

magic_items.name: The Black Arrow of Bard
magic_items.description: Type: Arrow. Craftsmanship: Dwarven (Erebor). Banes: Dragons. Enchanted Qualities: 1. Sure Shot 2. Superior Keen 3. Superior Fell. Notes: Said to have been forged in the Lonely Mountain, the Black Arrow was passed down the line of Girion until Bard the Bowman slew Smaug with it. Whether this is that same arrow is unknown, although many a Barding would claim it was so.

magic_items.name: Scatha's Tooth
magic_items.description: Type: Axe. Craftsmanship: Dwarven (Erebor). Banes: —. Enchanted Qualities: 1. Gleam of Terror 2. Fell 3. Curse of Weakness (Dragon-sickness). Notes: When Fram slew the Dragon Scatha, he took his hoard as his own, much to the dismay of the Dwarves of the Grey Mountains. As recompense he sent them a handful of the Dragon's teeth, one of which is embedded in the haft of this axe. Although the blade strikes true, something of the Dragon's greed remains about it.

magic_items.name: Biting-storm
magic_items.description: Type: Great Spear. Craftsmanship: Dwarven and Elven (Khazad-dûm and Eregion). Banes: Dragon. Qualities: 1. Superior Grievous 2. Fierce (see page 30). Notes: Forged in Khazad-dûm and wound with the spells of the Elves of Eregion, Biting-storm was fashioned with one purpose in mind: to pierce the heart of a terrible Dragon, whose name has long been lost to legend.

magic_items.name: Durin's Ring
magic_items.description: The first of the Seven Rings of Power given to the Dwarf lords, Durin's Ring was said to have been given to Durin III not by Sauron but by the Elves themselves. The ring was said to breed gold from gold, but it also inflamed the bearer's heart to greed. Durin's Ring was lost to the Necromancer, but what then became of it? (Greater Blessing of Investigation, Curse of Weakness)

magic_items.name: The Armour of Náin
magic_items.description:
Type: Ring-mail
Craftsmanship: Dwarven
Banes: n/a
Qualities: 1. Cunning Make 2. Rune-scored Armour
Notes: The force of the blow that Azog struck Náin was strong enough to break his neck, but it could not pierce his armour. Small comfort to the Dwarf, no doubt, but testimony to the craftsmanship of the smiths of the Iron Hills who made it.

magic_items.name: The Red Axe of Dáin
magic_items.description:
Type: Great Axe
Craftsmanship: Dwarven
Banes: n/a
Qualities: 1. Fell 2. Grievous 3. Gleam of Terror
Notes: Dáin slew Azog with a blow from his red axe, cutting his head off. But surely Dáin kept his axe when he returned to the Iron Hills; so why does this weapon bear his name, and a blade stained crimson with the blood of Orcs?

magic_items.name: Ironfoot Hauberk (Ring-mail)
magic_items.description: The ancient weaponsmiths of your folk possessed the secret of forging a hauberk of steel mail, made of a fine and flexible mesh that is especially comfortable and lightweight (for a suit of metal armour). You do not have Disadvantage on Stealth checks when wearing the Ironfoot Hauberk. Furthermore, if you have Dexterity of 12 or higher, the armour provides AC 15.

magic_items.name: Worm Axe
magic_items.description: A Worm Axe is a double-headed weapon used by the Dwarves in their wars against the Dragons. Its hooked end can bite into the armoured skin of a Great Worm. When a creature with a Weak Spot exposes it and you use your reaction to strike, you have Advantage on your attack roll.

features.name: Baruk Khazâd!
features.description: If the Stone Guard's attack reduces his target to 0 hit points, he may use his bonus action to move up to half of his speed and make another attack against a different target.

features.name: Old Hatred
features.description: When the Stone Guard is fighting Orc-kind with a melee weapon, he can re-roll his weapon's damage die and use either total.

actions.name: Axe
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 7 (1d8+3) slashing damage or 8 (1d10+3) slashing damage if used with two hands.

features.name: Khazâd ai-mênu!
features.description: If the Iron Guard's attack misses, he may use his bonus action to make another attack against the same target.

features.name: Warrior's Charge
features.description: The Iron Guard has Advantage on all attacks made in the first round of combat.

actions.name: Mattock
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 10 (2d6+3) piercing damage.

features.name: Secret Craft
features.description: The Smith can use his bonus action to gain Advantage on one ability check (including tools).

features.name: Stiff Necks
features.description: If one or more Smiths are present for an Audience and the speaker for the Company is not a Dwarf, the Introduction Check is made with Disadvantage.

actions.name: Hammer
actions.description: Melee or Thrown Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft or range 20/60 ft, one target. Hit: 4 (1d4+2) bludgeoning damage.

features.name: Baruk Khazâd!
features.description: If Dáin's attack reduces his target to 0 hit points, he may use his bonus action to move up to half of his speed and make another attack against a different target.

features.name: Khazâd ai-mênu!
features.description: If Dáin's attack misses, he may use his bonus action to attack the same target again.

features.name: Runes of Protection
features.description: Dáin's armour provides resistance to non-magical piercing damage (noted above).

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Dáin makes three attacks with his red axe.

actions.name: The Red Axe
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 13 (1d12+1d4+4) magical slashing damage (see page 112).

reactions.name: Great Might (Recharge 5-6)
reactions.description: Dáin may use his reaction when he takes damage from a melee or ranged weapon attack to reduce his damage taken by 4, to a minimum of 1 point of damage taken.

features.name: Stubborn
features.description: During an Audience or other meeting, the Smith imposes Disadvantage on Charisma checks made by the heroes.

actions.name: Hammer
actions.description: Melee or Thrown Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft or range 20/60 ft, one target. Hit: 5 (1d4+3) bludgeoning damage.

features.name: Confound
features.description: Courtiers are masters of turning an errant word into a deadly dagger to public opinion. In an Audience, the Courtier can force the spokesperson for the Company to make a DC 12 Charisma saving throw or gain Disadvantage on all further checks during the Audience.

features.name: Lord of His Domain
features.description: Courtiers only meet with adventurers in situations and places favorable to themselves. The Courtier imposes Disadvantage on the Introduction Check for an Audience.

features.name: Expert
features.description: Courtiers double their Proficiency Bonus for Persuasion and Traditions (included above).

actions.name: Dagger
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft or range 20/60 ft, one target. Hit: 3 (1d4+1) piercing damage.

features.name: Eagle-feathered Arrow (1/day)
features.description: As a bonus action the Royal Archer draws this special arrow and attacks with her Great Bow. A successful hit causes a critical hit and any creature Medium size or smaller must make a DC 15 Strength saving throw or become Prone.

features.name: Hawk’s Eye
features.description: The Royal Archer may use this ability as a bonus action. She does not suffer Disadvantage on attack rolls due to being at long range this turn.

actions.name: Volley-storm (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: The Royal Archer can use her action to make a ranged attack against any number of creatures within 10 ft of a point she can see within her weapon’s range. She must have ammunition for each target, as normal, and she makes a separate attack roll for each target.

actions.name: Great Bow
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, range 150/600 ft, one target. Hit: 8 (1d8+4) piercing damage.

features.name: Battle Brothers
features.description: If three or more guards are fighting the same enemy and that enemy has no allies engaged with the guards, the guards have Advantage on their attacks.

features.name: Silver Whistle
features.description: The guard can use his bonus reaction to summon help, which arrives at the end of his next turn. Roll 1d6: 1-4: that number of City Guards; 5: a Guard Commander; 6: a Royal Archer.

actions.name: Long sword
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 6 (1d8+2) slashing damage or 7 (1d10+2) slashing damage if used with both hands.

reactions.name: Tackle
reactions.description: When a creature moves out of the guard's reach, he may use his reaction to make a grapple attack with Advantage.

features.name: Hard Eyed
features.description: The Commander is a veteran of many battles and scores a critical hit on rolls of 18, 19 or 20.

features.name: Shield-strike (Recharge 5-6)
features.description: If the Commander deals damage with his longsword, he can use his bonus action to slam his great shield into the target. The creature takes 4 points of bludgeoning damage and must make a DC 13 Strength saving throw or become Prone.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The Commander makes two attacks with his longsword.

actions.name: Longsword
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 7 (1d8+3) slashing damage or 8 (1d10+3) slashing damage if used with both hands.

features.name: Baleful Mattock
features.description: Thorin scores a critical hit on a natural roll of 19 or 20.

features.name: Battle-charge
features.description: If Thorin moves at least half his speed to engage a new foe he gains Advantage on his attack rolls.

features.name: Guardian
features.description: Thorin can use his reaction to make an Opportunity Attack when a creature within reach attempts to move away from him. If he hits the creature, it does not move.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Thorin makes three attacks with his mattock.

actions.name: Mattock
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 11 (2d6+4) piercing damage.

features.name: Bulky Armour
features.description: Sark has Disadvantage on Dexterity checks.

features.name: Horrible Strength
features.description: If Sark makes a successful melee attack, he may use his bonus action to cause 3 additional damage to the target.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Sark makes two attacks with either his Orc-axe or long spear.

actions.name: Orc-axe
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 6 (1d6+3) slashing damage or 7 (1d8+3) slashing damage if wielded with two hands.

actions.name: Long Spear
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 10 ft, one target. Hit: 8 (1d10+3) piercing damage. Heavy, two-handed.

reactions.name: Counterattack (Recharge 5-6)
reactions.description: If an attack roll misses Sark, he can use his reaction to make an attack roll with Advantage. He must be wielding a melee weapon and able to see his attacker.

monsters.name: The Forest Dragon
languages: Unknown (no one in this Age of the world has heard her speak)

features.name: Mirkwood Dweller
features.description: As a bonus action, if the Forest Dragon is within Mirkwood she can gain half-cover from a scenery feature, even if it would not normally provide it.

features.name: Thing of Terror
features.description: As a bonus action, The Forest Dragon can rear up and display her full strength. Each creature within 60 ft must make a DC 19 Wisdom saving throw or be Frightened until the end of their next turn.

features.name: Tough Hide
features.description: The Forest Dragon is resistant to non-magical bludgeoning and slashing damage.

features.name: Weak Spot
features.description: If the Forest Dragon uses her Crushing Tail-grip any heroes that are within range may use their reaction to make a single attack. For this attack only, she loses her damage resistances and she is vulnerable to all piercing, slashing and bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The Forest Dragon makes one Bite and two Rend attacks.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +11 to hit, reach 10 ft, one target. Hit: 20 (3d8+7) piercing damage.

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +11 to hit, reach 10 ft, one target. Hit: 16 (2d8+7) slashing damage.

actions.name: Crushing Tail-grip
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +11 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 13 (1d12+7) bludgeoning damage. The target becomes Grappled (escape DC 21). The Dragon can spend its action to cause 13 (1d12+7) bludgeoning damage to the Grappled foe.

legendary_actions.name: Deadly Tail-grip
legendary_actions.description: The Forest Dragon causes 13 (1d12+7) bludgeoning damage to a Grappled foe.

features.name: Fell Speed
features.description: Kibiluzn may take a bonus action to Disengage and move up to his speed towards an enemy he can see.

features.name: Hatred (Dwarves, Recharge 5-6)
features.description: Kibiluzn can use his bonus action to gain Advantage on attacks against his chosen prey this round.

features.name: Weak Spot
features.description: If Kibiluzn uses a special Feature that uses an action (Noxious Vapours), any heroes that are within range may use their reaction to make a single attack. For this attack only, he is vulnerable to Piercing, Slashing and Bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 10 ft, one target. Hit: 15 (2d8+6) piercing damage or 17 (2d8+8) damage at night or underground.

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 10 ft, one target. Hit: 12 (2d6+5) slashing damage or 14 (2d6+7) damage at night or underground.

actions.name: Noxious Vapours (Recharge 4-6)
actions.description: As an action, Kibiluzn exhales a thick cloud of foul fumes in a 15 ft cone. Each creature within the cone must make a DC 16 Constitution saving throw, becoming Blinded and Poisoned for 3 (1d4+1) rounds on a failure or Poisoned for 3 (1d4+1) rounds on a success.

reactions.name: Commanding Voice
reactions.description: Kibiluzn demands utter loyalty from the Orcs and Goblins in his employ. As a reaction, Kibiluzn can utter a command or shout a warning whenever an allied creature that he can see within 30 ft, is about to make an attack roll or a saving throw. The target can add a d6 Command Die to its next roll, provided it can hear and understand the message. A creature can benefit from only one Command Die at a time, and creatures that possess Commanding Voice cannot benefit from this effect.

features.name: Fleet of Wing
features.description: Lytegan's flying speed is 90 ft.

features.name: Scaly Hide
features.description: Lytegan is resistant to non-magical bludgeoning and piercing damage.

features.name: Weak Spot
features.description: If Lytegan uses a special ability that uses an action (Fire Breath), any heroes that are within range may use their reaction to make a single attack. For this attack only, she loses any damage resistances and is vulnerable to Piercing, Slashing and Bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 10 ft, one target. Hit: 15 (2d8+6) piercing damage.

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 10 ft, one target. Hit: 13 (2d6+6) slashing damage.

actions.name: Fire Breath (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: As an action, Lytegan exhales fire in a 30-ft cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw, taking 31 (9d6) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

legendary_actions.name: Piercing Words
legendary_actions.description: Lytegan can force a hidden creature to make a DC 18 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure the creature reveals itself to her. She must be able to infer the presence of the creature in some way (for example, she can hear the creature or it was in sight recently) in order to use this ability.

legendary_actions.name: Wing Attack
legendary_actions.description: Lytegan can beat her wings. Each creature within 15 ft of her must make a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw or take 13 (2d6+6) bludgeoning damage and be knocked Prone. She can then fly up to half her flying speed.

features.name: Horrible Strength
features.description: If Raenar makes a successful melee attack, he may use his bonus action to cause 7 additional damage of the same type as the original type.

features.name: Weak Spot
features.description: If Raenar uses a special ability that uses an action (Mesmerise or Poison Blast), any heroes that are within range may use their reaction to make a single attack. For this attack only, Raenar is vulnerable to Piercing, Slashing and Bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Raenar makes two attacks biting once and then either rending or using his tail attack.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +12 to hit, reach 10 ft, one target. Hit: 20 (3d8+7) piercing damage.

actions.name: Rend
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +12 to hit, reach 10 ft, one target. Hit: 18 (2d10+7) slashing damage.

actions.name: Tail-Lash
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +12 to hit, reach 10 ft, one target. Hit: 13 (1d12+7) bludgeoning damage and the target is knocked Prone.

actions.name: Mesmerise
actions.description: Raenar may use his action and target one creature, who must make a DC 18 Wisdom saving throw or become Charmed by the Dragon. Each time he does anything harmful to the target, it can repeat the saving throw, ending the effect on a success. Otherwise, the effect lasts 24 hours or until Raenar leaves the area, is slain or takes a bonus action to end the effect.

actions.name: Poison Blast (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: As an action, Raenar exhales poisonous bile in a 50 ft cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 18 Dexterity saving throw, taking 37 (5d4+25) poison damage and becoming Poisoned for 2d4 rounds on failed saving throw. A successful saving throw reduces the damage by half, and the target is Poisoned for only 1d4 rounds.

reactions.name: Draconic Resistance (Recharge 5-6)
reactions.description: Dragons are notoriously tough and free-willed. Raenar may activate this ability as a reaction to failing a saving throw. He automatically succeeds at the saving throw instead.

npcs.name: Munin, Keeper of Records
npcs.description: A venerable Dwarf of many winters, Munin is the head archivist of the Chamber of Marzabul under Erebor. Lore of the elder days that exists nowhere else in the North, save perhaps the halls of Rivendell, lies within his charge. Companions with the support of King Dáin, or another noteworthy Dwarf, may be able to get his assistance in researching old records, as his memory remains quite sharp, though he is short with outsiders and any he considers to be wasting his time. Munin has a long white beard that just touches the floor. Unfortunately, despite his amazing grasp of ancient lore, dealing with Munin can be trying; at his advanced age (well over 200) his hearing is failing, however, he refuses to accept this and abhors shouting as he believes it implies disrespect.

npcs.name: Roäc the Raven
npcs.description: The chief of the great ravens of Ravenhill, Roäc is ancient even for one of his kind. When Thorin and company came to Erebor for vengeance upon Smaug, Roäc was already more than 150 years old, and marked by age. It was Roäc who flew to Thorin's Company with news that Smaug had been slain by Bard the Bowman, and who sent his ravens to Dáin of the Iron Hills with word to bring reinforcements to protect the treasure of Erebor. The son of Carc, said by the Dwarves to be the greatest lord of the ravens ever to have lived, Roäc has inherited much of his noble father's wisdom. He rightly warned Thorin that the treasure that had brought him to Erebor would be his death, and even now is a trusted ally and counsellor to the Dwarves. Roäc is now so ancient that he rarely leaves his mountainside nest, but his ravens range

npcs.name: Roäc

features.name: Motivation
features.description: Of highest importance is the safety of the Mountain.

features.name: Expectations
features.description: +1 if the Company announces that they will abide by Roäc's advice — he's used to stubborn Dwarves and pleased that his wisdom does not fall on deaf ears. -2 if they do not treat him as an equal — despite his great age his knowledge is vast.

npcs.description: The son of Carc, said by the Dwarves to be the greatest lord of the ravens ever to have lived, Roäc has inherited much of his noble father's wisdom. He rightly warned Thorin that the treasure that had brought him to Erebor would be his death, and even now is a trusted ally and counsellor to the Dwarves. Roäc is now so ancient that he rarely leaves his mountainside nest, but his ravens range far and see all — there is no movement within the north of Wilderland that Roäc does not know of.

npcs.name: Glóin the Emissary

features.name: Motivation
features.description: I am a representative of King Dáin and I will bear myself accordingly, no matter the situation.

features.name: Expectations
features.description: +1 if the Company expressing willingness to compromise — Gloin knows that diplomacy is built on both parties giving up a little; -2 if they have a Elf of Mirkwood as their speaker — Gloin has never forgotten his rough treatment at their hands.

features.name: Customisation
features.description: Add Persuasion +5 to the Dwarf-Lord's list of skills to represent Gloin. In battle he wields the Axe Under the Mountain (Superior Fell, Gleam of Terror).

equipment: Axe Under the Mountain (Superior Fell, Gleam of Terror)
npcs.description: The skill of most Dwarves, it is said, lies in their hands, whether they are wielding tools or weapons. While Glóin is a veteran of a great many battles, and can swing an axe with the best of them, his tongue is his truest tool and weapon. Since the Battle of Five Armies, Glóin has swiftly become one of the most favoured of Dáin's envoys. He is trusted to advance the interests of the Lonely Mountain in such a way as to make Erebor's position clear, while not unduly upsetting allies. A trying position, but Glóin does it with grace, even on the rare occasions when he has to deal with Wood Elves, who he regards poorly. Glóin serves as the Kingdom under the Mountain's main ambassador to Esgaroth. He has a well-appointed mansion in Lake-town where he spends several weeks a year, working on a wide variety of trade issues with the Men of the Lake. His valiant son Gimli regularly accompanies him on his journeys on Erebor's behalf. Glóin is exceedingly well-spoken and generally kindly to all (save Wood Elves). Glóin favours white garments, or brightly coloured ones trimmed with white, matching the colour of his forked beard.

npcs.name: Óin the Healer

features.name: Motivation
features.description: Are you friend or foe? Do you oppose the King under the Mountain? Answer quickly, for you have an impatient Dwarf in your face!

features.name: Expectations
features.description: +1 if the heroes answer directly without bluster; +2 if they are willing to laugh at themselves

features.name: Customisation
features.description: Add Medicine +5 to the Dwarf-Lord to represent Ori's skill with herbs.

npcs.description: Óin is Glóin's older brother. The two have little in common, save their knack for building fires and their love for one another. Where Glóin is subtle, Óin is blunt. Where Glóin can make even the most unpleasant news easier to hear, Óin is brutally, painfully honest. Far more belligerent than his younger brother, Óin remains a fierce warrior but a skilled healer. His expertise with herbs, potions and salves is profound, almost rivalling that of the Elves of Rivendell. Like his brother, Óin too, has become an emissary for Dain, but Óin is typically sent on longer journeys to folk who prefer action to fair speech. Óin has a sharp sense of humour, though he skewers himself as readily as others he meets on the road. Óin keeps his beard short, a habit he developed after a particularly unpleasant encounter with spiders in Mirkwood. He favours brown garments, the better to go unnoticed in the Wild.

npcs.name: Bifur the Trader

features.name: Motivation
features.description: I am looking for trustworthy sorts who are willing to brave the Wild on behalf of the King.

features.name: Expectations
features.description: +2 if the Company are well-worn — Bifur cares little for fancy clothes or exquisite manners; -1 if they're shy about money matters — he expects to pay for good service, though not too much, of course.

features.name: Customisation
features.description: Add "Walking Songs. If the companions travel with Bifur, once upon the journey they can make a DC 10 Charisma (Performance) check. If successful, the hero gains Inspiration." to the Dwarf-Lord entry.

equipment: elaborately carved walking cane bound with strands of Mithril
npcs.description: Bifur is the son of a smith from the Iron Hills and a far-travelled Dwarf, who has seen much of the North and the West. After the Battle of Five Armies, Bifur took on a position as one of Dáin's emissaries to Erebor's trading partners. He now spends much of his time travelling between Ironthorpe, near the Iron Hills, and the Lonely Mountain, ensuring that the regular shipments of ore that move along the road between the two don't go 'astray'. Bifur is a sturdy middle-aged Dwarf with silver streaking his black beard. He carries an elaborately carved walking cane bound with strands of Mithril, a family heirloom, though his mattock is often near to hand as well. Bifur occasionally needs the help of adventurous sorts to guard especially valuable shipments or look into unusual matters he has heard about on the road. Bifur tends to speak in quick bursts of words, saying several things at once in rapid succession, before falling silent for an uncomfortably long amount of time afterwards.

npcs.name: Bofur the Miner
npcs.description: Bifur's cousin and Bombur's brother, Bofur was raised in the hard environs of the Blue Mountains. A miner and occasional explorer, Bofur developed a real thirst for adventure during his travels with Thorin's Company. Favouring his mattock in battle, Bofur proved himself a skilled warrior, time and again fighting fearlessly to protect his king.

npcs.name: Bombur

features.name: Expertise
features.description: Bombur doubles his Proficiency Bonus for certain skills, noted above.

features.name: Riddling Words
features.description: If Bombur spends 10 minutes with a creature, it must succeed at a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw or become Charmed until Bombur gives the creature a reason to doubt his sincerity or it takes a long rest.

features.name: Sneak Attack
features.description: Once per turn, Bombur deals an extra 3 (1d6) damage when he hits a target with a weapon attack and has Advantage on the attack roll, or the target is within 5 feet of an ally and he doesn't have Disadvantage on the attack roll.

actions.name: Short Sword
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 7 (1d6+4) magical piercing damage.

npcs.description: Bofur's brother and Bifur's cousin, Bombur's immense size and voracious appetite caused frequent problems on the Quest for Erebor, but his culinary skills and uncanny ability to sniff out provisions in the unlikeliest of environments along with his jolly nature made his presence essential to the morale of the party. Bombur is a well-known and beloved figure in both Dale and Erebor, a frequent guest in the dining halls and kitchens of both kingdoms. Since the Battle of Five Armies, he has dedicated himself to ensuring that good food is readily available in the North and has quietly backed several spice merchants and taverns.

npcs.name: Balin

features.name: Chinks in the Armour
features.description: Balin can use his bonus action to make a Wisdom (Perception) check against the AC of his target. If he succeeds, his first successful attack roll this round counts as a critical hit.

features.name: Expert
features.description: Balin doubles his Proficiency Bonus for Perception and Traditions (included above).

features.name: Khazâd ai-mênu!
features.description: If Balin's attack misses, he may use his bonus action to make another attack against the same target.

features.name: Old Hatred
features.description: When Balin is fighting Orc-kind with a melee weapon, he can re-roll his weapon's damage die and use either total.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Balin makes three attacks with his great axe.

actions.name: Great Axe
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 9 (1d12+3) slashing damage.

npcs.description: Balin is a renowned Dwarf of Thorin's Company, now a lord of Erebor. He is wise and perceptive, with a deep hatred of Orcs.

npcs.name: Dwalin

features.name: Leadership
features.description: As a bonus action, Dwalin can command a nearby Dwarf other than himself to act. That Dwarf takes its turn immediately after Dwalin.

features.name: Old Hatred
features.description: When Dwalin is fighting Orc-kind with a melee weapon, he can re-roll his weapon's damage die and use either total.

features.name: Unyielding
features.description: Dwalin can use his bonus action to gain 10 temporary hit points.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Dwalin makes three attacks with his great axe.

actions.name: Great Axe
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 9 (1d12+3) slashing damage

npcs.description: Dwalin is a ruthless and skilled warrior, staunch supporter of Thorin Oakenshield, and informal head of the Stone Guard.

npcs.name: Bard the Dragon-slayer, King of Dale

features.name: Audience with the King
features.description: Hard-voiced and frequently of sombre mood, Bard is a proud, practical man, shaped by his former life as a captain. He is widely famed for being true to his word, no matter the personal cost. The Bowman reads hearts well, and is quick to see the worth of an individual. King Bard can most frequently be found in the Royal Palace, though he occasionally wanders the Market Square, with bodyguard in tow. When the crown grows heavy, he leaves the city to hunt on horseback in the lands to the west. Bard is a tall, imposing man, hale even as the years add increasing amounts of silver to his once black hair, with a sharp glance and a taciturn manner. Only his queen has the knack of getting him to smile regularly.

features.name: Motivation
features.description: I have great ambitions for Dale: to make a kingdom in the North that all may see as a shining example of the Free Peoples’ best qualities.

features.name: Expectations
features.description: +1 if the heroes bring important news to King Bard; -3 if they ply him with unwise courtesies or spurious allegations.

features.name: Bard as a Patron
features.description: The Bowman concerns himself far more with action than words. Those who accept his patronage are not likely to find themselves at court much. Many of the tasks that Bard will ask of his followers involve furthering his ambitions by advancing the interests of Dale or occasionally by assisting his allies. This will likely see the Company sent into the wild to investigate monstrous threats or lending their weapons to defend a far-flung settlement from raiders. Bard can be made a patron of the Company if they have directly aided him during an Adventuring phase. Characters who have Bard as their patron may choose

npcs.description: Bard the Dragon-slayer, King of Dale. A grim but worthy man; stern but forthright in word and deed. Widely regarded as a good king, not easily swayed by idle politics and ever mindful of the welfare of his people.

npcs.name: King Bard

features.name: Disciplined
features.description: Bard may use his bonus action to grant himself Advantage on all attack rolls this round.

features.name: Eagle-feathered Arrow
features.description: As a bonus action Bard draws this special arrow and attacks with his Great Bow. A successful hit causes a critical hit and any creature Medium size or smaller must make a DC 17 Strength saving throw or become Prone.

features.name: Hard Eyed
features.description: Bard scores a critical hit on rolls of 18, 19 or 20.

features.name: Hawk's Eye
features.description: Bard may use this ability as a bonus action. He does not suffer Disadvantage on attack rolls due to being at long range this turn.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Bard makes three attacks with his great bow.

actions.name: Great Bow
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, range 150/600 ft, one target. Hit: 9 (1d8+5) piercing damage.

npcs.description: King Bard, the Dragon-slayer, ruler of Dale. A grim, socially reticent king who can be made a patron of the Company.

npcs.name: Elstan, First Captain of Dale

features.name: Aegis of Dale
features.description: Elstan bears a magical shield forged in Erebor for the protection of the new kingdom. While he bears it, he has Advantage on death saving throws and can use his bonus action to gain 10 temporary hit points.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Elstan makes two longsword attacks.

actions.name: Longsword (Bitter Birthright)
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 9 (1d8+5) piercing damage.

reactions.name: Commanding Voice
reactions.description: Elstan may use his reaction to utter a command when a non-hostile creature he can see within 30 ft is about to make an attack roll or a saving throw. The target adds a d6 Command Die to that roll, provided it can understand the message. A creature can benefit from only one Command Die at a time, and creatures that possess Commanding Voice cannot benefit.

reactions.name: Parry
reactions.description: Elstan adds 2 to his AC against one melee attack that would hit him. He must be aware of the incoming attack in order to parry.

npcs.description: Among the first to swear loyalty to King Bard, Elstan is a widely famed, and beloved, warrior. Ever at the forefront of battles and swift to offer aid to beset farmers, Elstan spends almost as much time in the Upper Marches as he does in Dale. Elstan commands the Royal Barracks and sets the example that many of the Royal Archers strive to emulate. Ironically, he's only a passing archer, but he is a master swordsman.

npcs.name: Brindal, Enterprising Thief

features.name: Expert
features.description: Brindal doubles her Proficiency Bonus for Sleight of Hand and Stealth.

features.name: Nimble Escape
features.description: Brindal can take the Disengage or Hide action as a bonus action on each of her turns.

features.name: Sneak Attack
features.description: Once per turn, Brindal deals an extra 3 (1d6) damage when she hits a target with a weapon attack and has Advantage on the attack roll, or when the target is within 5 ft of an ally of Brindal that isn't Incapacitated and she doesn't have Disadvantage on the attack roll.

actions.name: Short Sword
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 7 (1d6+4) piercing damage

reactions.name: Snake-like Speed
reactions.description: Brindal is adept at avoiding injury and can use her reaction to halve the attack damage on an attack that she is aware of.

npcs.description: Though the people of Dale are widely thought to be true and noble, not all aspire to honourable lives. Brindal is a young woman who lost much when Lake-town burned. Barely fifteen when the fires claimed her family, she followed many of her people to find a new home in Dale. Bitterness crept into her heart as riches finally began to flow into the city, but only a little silver found its way to her. Now, Brindal seeks to fill the emptiness left by the loss of her family and all she held dear with hoarded gold. She leads a small band of thieves based out of the Brokenstone who regularly ply the streets of Dale, picking the pockets of idle shoppers and keeping an ear out for useful secrets she can parley to interested parties. She has begun to hold Bardings in contempt, and the darkness of her spirit deepens with every season.

npcs.name: Brindal

features.name: Snake-like Speed
features.description: Brindal is adept at avoiding injury and can use her reaction to halve the attack damage on an attack that she is aware of.

actions.name: Short Sword
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 7 (1d6+4) piercing damage

npcs.description: Brindal is a companion with the Snake-like Speed reaction. She is within 5 ft of an ally of Brindal that isn't Incapacitated and she doesn't have Disadvantage on the attack roll.

npcs.name: Lord Bryni

features.name: Iron Will
features.description: Bryni is haughty and his heart has grown cold. If the heroes have accrued any negative modifiers in an audience with him, the Final Audience check is made with Disadvantage.

features.name: Savage Assault
features.description: When Bryni rolls a natural 18 or 19, he may, as a bonus action, make a single additional melee attack against the same opponent.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Bryni makes two attacks with his long sword.

actions.name: Long Sword
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 7 (1d8+3) slashing damage or 8 (1d10+3) slashing damage if used with two hands.

npcs.description: Lord Bryni is a haughty noble who resembles the hero he aspires to be, with long flowing dark hair, a proud, lordly gaze, and a habit for wearing shining mail and red cloaks even when not dressing for battle.

npcs.name: Garrick

features.name: Bodyguards
features.description: Garrick is always surrounded by Thugs and Outlaws whose duty it is to protect their leader. At least one Thug or Outlaw in his retinue gains the Thrall (Garrick) special reaction ability (see below).

features.name: Nimble Escape
features.description: Garrick can take the Disengage or Hide action as a bonus action on each of his turns.

actions.name: Broadsword
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 8 (1d8+4) slashing damage.

actions.name: Great Bow
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, range 150/600 ft, one target. Hit: 8 (1d8+4) piercing damage.

npcs.description: Garrick is a short, furrow-browed man with little time to bandy words with civilised folk. He is eager to whet his weapons with the blood of those who threaten the land.

npcs.name: Hakon, Barding Noble

features.name: Motivation
features.description: Only by valour and force can the North be free — diplomacy and contrition are but ways for our enemies to worm their way into our hearts.

features.name: Expectations
features.description: +1 if the Company are the sort who prefer problems that can be solved with quick and decisive sword-work; +2 if they are mostly Men-folk (Hakon has little trust for Dwarves or Elves); -2 if they seem the type to ask too many questions and poke into dark corners.

npcs.description: Once a powerful merchant of Esgaroth, now a courtier of Dale. Hakon's family directly descends from the noble bloodlines of Dale. In his late forties with long, grey hair, Hakon dresses in what finery he can still afford and plays the part of the loyal courtier; but while he smiles freely, his eyes betray nothing but contempt.

npcs.name: Lord Hakon

features.name: Expert
features.description: Hakon doubles his Proficiency Bonus for his skills (included above).

features.name: Twisted Words
features.description: Lord Hakon is never far from his own followers and even commands the respect (so far) of the City Guard. If attacked in a public place, he can spend his bonus action to summon appropriate aid, which arrives at the end of his next turn. Slaying those who believe they’re saving Hakon from banditry is a Misdeed worthy of several Shadow points.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Hakon makes three attacks with his sword.

actions.name: Long Sword
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 6 (1d8+2) slashing damage or 7 (1d10+2) slashing damage if wielded with two hands.

npcs.description: Lord Hakon is a cunning and deceptive human noble who commands respect and wields a long sword in battle.

npcs.name: Rugash the Serpent, Orc-Chieftain

features.name: Stealthy
features.description: Rugash may use his bonus action each round to Hide.

features.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
features.description: While in sunlight, Rugash has disadvantage on attack rolls, as well as on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Rugash makes two attacks with his scimitar or his whip.

actions.name: Orcish Scimitar
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 9 (2d4+4) slashing damage. Two-handed.

actions.name: Whip
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 10 ft, one target. Hit: 4 (1d4+2) slashing damage.

actions.name: Call for Aid
actions.description: Rugash always keeps a few of his lads back in case of trouble. He can use his action to summon them. 2d4 Orc Soldiers arrive in 1d4+1 rounds. If Rugash is slain before they arrive, they will likely avoid the Company unless the Loremaster deems otherwise.

npcs.description: Rugash is a cunning and subtle Orc chieftain who leads a successful tribe on the Waste, known for his stealth and strategic mind.

npcs.name: Erna

features.name: Battle-fury
features.description: Erna can use her bonus action to enter a Fury. While in this state, she has Advantage on Strength checks and saving throws, gains +4 damage to her attacks and has resistance to non-magical bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage. It ends after 1 minute or if she is Unconscious, or ends her turn without having attacked a hostile creature or taken damage since her previous turn.

features.name: Dragon-touched
features.description: Erna has Advantage on any saving throws caused by Dragons. Any Intelligence (Lore) checks that she makes about Dragons are at Advantage as well.

features.name: Reckless
features.description: Erna may choose to gain Advantage on all attacks she makes in a round, but all attacks on her gain Advantage until the start of her next turn.

features.name: Region-lore (The Waste)
features.description: If Erna is with the Company for a journey that begins or ends in the Waste, the Guide rolls 1d8+4 for the Embarkation Roll.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Erna makes two attacks with her spear or great bow.

actions.name: Spear
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft or range 20/60 ft, one target. Hit: 7 (1d6+4) piercing damage or 8 (1d8+4) piercing damage if used with two hands to make a melee attack.

actions.name: Great Bow
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, range 150/600 ft, one target. Hit: 5 (1d8+1) piercing damage.

npcs.description: Erna is a vengeful hunter who lost her family to Smaug and now stalks the Waste seeking dragon lairs, driven by rage and a desire for revenge.

npcs.name: Ellaras

features.name: Desperate
features.description: If Ellaras begins his turn with 33 or less hit points, he gains Advantage on all his attack rolls.

features.name: Expert
features.description: Ellaras doubles his Proficiency Bonus for Perception and Survival (included above).

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Ellaras makes two attacks with his dagger or bow.

actions.name: Dagger
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft or range 20/60, one target. Hit: 6 (1d4+4) piercing damage.

actions.name: Bow
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, range 80/320 ft, one target. Hit: 8 (1d8+4) piercing damage.

npcs.description: Long ago, as Men reckon time, Ellaras was part of a company of Elves that set forth from the Woodland Realm on a quest of great secrecy into the Emyn Duir, the Mountains of Mirkwood. Ellaras was found, months later, poisoned and raving, his hair white and his eyes wild, near the borders of the Woodland Realm. Now Ellaras searches for something amidst the abandoned Dwarf-holds of the Grey Mountains.

npcs.name: Galion

features.name: Deadly Shot
features.description: At the start of his turn, Galion may use his bonus action to aim. His speed becomes 0. If he does so then he has Advantage on all ranged weapon attacks he makes this round.

features.name: Hawk's Eye
features.description: Galion may use this ability as a bonus action. He does not suffer Disadvantage on attack rolls due to being at long range this turn.

features.name: Hunter
features.description: Galion doubles his Proficiency Bonus for Perception checks (included above).

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Galion can make two attacks with either his Short Sword or his Great Bow.

actions.name: Short Sword
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 7 (1d6+4) piercing damage.

actions.name: Great Bow
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, range 150/600 ft, one target. Hit: 8 (1d8+4) piercing damage.

npcs.description: Once the personal cupbearer of the Elf-King, Galion is was consigned to the Long Marshes for drunkenness since the famous escape of a group of Dwarves from the royal halls. Now he and a small band of Mirkwood Elves patrol the marshes and make sure that none of its dangerous inhabitants make their way into the lands of Thranduil.

npcs.name: Loore

features.name: Focused
features.description: Loore displays amazing discipline in combat. He has 3 Focus points, which he regains when he takes a short or long rest. He can use his bonus action and spend one Focus point on his turn to take the Dash, Disengage or Dodge action or to make another attack with his great spear.

features.name: Grey Hawk
features.description: In combat, Loore can use his bonus action to command his friend to aid him against all attackers. Until the start of his next turn, all attack rolls against him are at Disadvantage. The Grey Hawk is too quick and clever to be the target of any normal attack.

features.name: Expert
features.description: Loore doubles his Proficiency Bonus for Perception and Survival (included above).

actions.name: Great Spear
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 9 (1d12+3) piercing damage.

npcs.description: A hunter of the Nether Marches, Loore regularly wanders over the wide grasslands, going wherever the wind or his mood takes him. A tracker without peer, there is nowhere on the steppes to flee where Loore cannot eventually follow. Loore keeps several birds of prey near him at all times, most often a beautiful grey hawk and a small prairie falcon. He also keeps a great secret, for Loore is a direct descendant of the ancient kings of old and he speaks the languages of all birds.

npcs.name: Móna, Daughter of Ginar

features.name: Tools for War
features.description: You have proficiency with axes, hand-axes, great axes, hammers, mattocks and warhammers.

features.name: Proficiencies
features.description: Proficient with miner's tools and flute

features.name: Languages
features.description: You can speak, read, and write Dalish, which is the tongue of the Bardings, who speak an older version of the Common Tongue. You can also speak, read and write the secret language of your people, which has never been shared with others.

features.name: Hardened
features.description: Part of the reason that you have accepted your fate is that you have seen too much death and misfortune already. It's your turn.

features.name: Enemy-lore (Orc-kind)
features.description: Not only are you doomed to die, but you are sure by whose hands it will be. You won't make it easy for them.

features.name: Night Vision
features.description: you can see in dim light 60 ft as bright light, but cannot see in the dark

features.name: Dwarven Resilience
features.description: You have Advantage on saving throws against poison, and you have resistance against poison damage.

features.name: Stonecunning
features.description: Whenever you make an Intelligence (History) check related to the origin of stonework, you are considered proficient in the History skill and add double your Proficiency Bonus to the check, instead of your normal Proficiency Bonus.

features.name: Dark Foreboding
features.description: You can get some sense of the Shadow's presence. You might be able to sense if an Orc warband is part of a larger force or if a particular ruin is blighted by the Enemy.

features.name: Great Weapon Fighting
features.description: When you roll a 1 or 2 for damage on your great axe, you can reroll the damage die. You must keep the new result.

features.name: Second Wind
features.description: On your turn you can use your bonus action to regain 1d10+1 hit points. You must take a short or long rest before using this again.

actions.name: Great Axe
actions.description: Atk Bonus +4, Damage 1d12+2 slashing

actions.name: Short Bow
actions.description: Atk Bonus +4, Damage 1d6+2 piercing. You can shoot your short bow up to 80 feet, or up to 320 feet with Disadvantage.

equipment: travelling gear for the current season
npcs.description: Móna, Daughter of Ginar, is a stout warrior of the Iron Hills who fought at the Battle of Five Armies in the host of Dáin Ironfoot. She is doomed to die and seeks to inspire her company by her selfless example.

features.name: Born to the Road
features.description: When beginning a journey where you serve as Guide for the Company, you may spend Inspiration instead of making an Embarkation Roll. You may choose one of the following results: Fine Weather, Paths Both Swift and True or Hidden from the Shadow.

features.name: Pathetic and Bedraggled
features.description: Folks often take pity on you and offer you a meal or a safe place to stay.

features.name: Known lands
features.description: You have 6 regions that you know well. See page 82 of the Player's Guide for more information.

features.name: Ways of the Wild
features.description: You have Advantage on Survival checks to track someone and can fill in for any missing journey roles.

features.name: Cultural Virtue
features.description: None.

actions.name: Mattock
actions.description: +4 to hit, 2d6 +2 piercing

actions.name: Great Bow
actions.description: +2 to hit, 1d8 piercing. You can shoot your great bow up to 150 feet, or up to 600 feet with Disadvantage.

equipment: travelling gear for the current season
npcs.description: You grew up wandering the Grey Mountain Narrows, ever in the shadow of your ancestral home. Occasionally you mustered up the courage to venture into the mountains themselves, delving in empty caves and holes, trading what you brought down from the mountains with the Men of Lake-town. Now, with Erebor rebuilt, you wonder if somewhere, deep in the mountains, the mansion of your kin might also be regained, and you seek out a company of heroes to aid you in your search.
